playstyle.role: Robot pet-master, aura platform and the game's tradeskill profession: one big bot does the damage and holds aggro while the Engineer runs a team aura, keeps shields, reflects and absorbs up, and builds the gear.
playstyle.summary: The Engineer (profession 3) summons a single robot and fights through it. Unlike the Meta-Physicist's three pets drawn from three different nano schools, EVERY Engineer bot reads exactly two skills - Matter Creation and Time & Space - at the SAME value, from Feeble Automaton (MC>4 / TS>4) up to the Widowmaker Battle Drone (MC>1895 / TS>1890). Around that it runs one friendly aura (EngineerAuras, strain 227, 15 nanos) or one hostile aura (EngineerDebuffAuras, strain 236, 14 nanos) - both needing MC + Matter Metamorphosis + Time & Space at the same value - plus the Assurance / Gift of Assurance team armor line, damage shields, reflect cocoons and 12 special-attack absorbers. It is also the only profession with Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Quantum FT, Weapon Smithing AND Tutoring all at cost factor 1.0, stacked with two profession perk lines, an AI perk line and its own +80/+125/+200 tradeskill buff nanos.
strengths: One skill pair runs the whole pet game: every bot summon needs only Matter Creation + Time & Space, both at cost factor 1.0 - far simpler and cheaper than the MP's three-school pet spread
Team auras: 15 friendly Sympathetic auras (strain 227) and 14 hostile Disruptive auras (strain 236) covering AC, reflect, damage shield, arms and negator effects

The best tradeskill profession in the data: ME/EE/QFT/Weapon Smithing/Tutoring all at cost 1.0, plus Gadgeteer, Mechanic, Tinkerer, Illogical Patterns (+160 to five tradeskills) and The Unknown Factor (+160 to four more), plus Knowledge (+80), Mastery (+125) and Engineer Composite Specialist Tradeskills (273346, +200 ME/EE/QFT)
A pet-repair line (Quick Fix through A Maker's Touch, plus Master's Repairs) and the Repair Pet perk action keep the bot alive with no healer
Strong defensive toolkit for a caster: Bio Shielding perk actions, ReflectShield / ShadowlandReflectBase cocoons, damage shields and 12 special-attack absorbers (strain 286)
Team travel: Beacon Warp / Team Beacon Warp and Shadowland Safeguard recall
Pistol is its cheapest weapon skill (1.5) and the Engineer has profession-only pistols and grenade launchers, so its own weapon damage is not an afterthought the way the MP's is
weaknesses: Only ONE bot at a time - lose it and you have no damage and no tank until you re-summon
No self-heal nano at all: the Engineer heals its BOT, not itself. Personal survivability is Bio Shielding perk actions, reflects/absorbs and raw HP
Psychological Modification and Sensory Improvement cost 2.4 each yet gate every tradeskill and weapon buff - an awkward, expensive second axis alongside MC/TS/MM
Evade-ClsC costs 4.0 (an MP pays 1.6) and Dodge-Rng 2.5, so close-combat evades are effectively unaffordable
Nano Pool costs 1.8 (an MP or NT pays 1.0) while bots and auras are expensive to cast
Only one aura runs at a time - friendly or hostile, not both
Tradeskills are an IP trap: the AOWiki Engineer Guide warns they are "a massive drain on IP" and that "there is no such thing as a Trade skill only engineer"
tips: Train Matter Creation and Time & Space in lockstep - a bot checks both at the same number, so one point of MC above TS is wasted.
Matter Metamorphosis is the third aura skill: MC + MM + TS at the same value. For the top aura (Sympathetic Fortress Screen 154562 / Null Space Disruptor 154725, ~870 each) MM has to keep pace.

Fund PM and SI to a chosen buff TIER, not to max: the Knowledge nanos want ~468-545 PM/SI for +80, the Mastery nanos ~817-854 for +125, and Engineer Composite Specialist Tradeskills wants 1033 for +200.
Take Mechanic to rank 3 early - it grants Repair Pet, an instant pet heal that costs no nano.
Bio Shielding is the survivability line for a class with no self-heal; AO-Universe notes most players run a reflect and a damage shield "from the Bioshield perk line or from buffs".
Your Run Speed sets your bot's - AO-Universe MKIII: "The runspeed of your pets is your own runspeed*1.2". Pet commands only reach 50 m.
Do not summon a bot while nano-debuffed - the bot is built at the skill level you had when you cast it.
Champion of Nano Combat is the strongest AI perk line for an Engineer: +100 to all six nano schools, including both bot skills.
Illogical Patterns + The Unknown Factor give +160 across nine tradeskills between them and are both open to Engineer - take them before any melee or off-profile AI line.
The FalseProfession nanos named "...Profession: Engineer" are AGENT nanos (they require Profession == 5) that make an Agent look like an Engineer. An Engineer cannot cast them.

breed.reasoning: Every Engineer bot is gated on Matter Creation and Time & Space, and AOWiki's Engineer:Breed_and_Skills states Intelligence provides "80% base ability of many nano skills", that Nanomage "works well for an engineer; they have better nano skills and intelligence", and that Atrox Int and nano skills are "poor". Local reference/breeds.json backs this: Nanomage has the highest trained Int and Psychic caps (512/512), 4 Max Nano per Nano Pool point (vs 3 Solitus, 2 Atrox) and a 55% nano-cost-reduction cap - which matters because the Engineer pays 1.8 for Nano Pool. The cost is fragility: 2 HP per Body Development point and the lowest Strength/Stamina caps. AO-Universe's Engineer Guide MKIII agrees for most of the game - Nanomage is "Best at early and mid-game (up to TL5 probably)".

alternatives.note: The safe default. AO-Universe MKIII: "With good HP and nanoskills mix probably the best overall breed for the average player, not looking for unique advantages." The AOWiki Engineer Guide uses Solitus as the baseline and advises raising "Agility and Stamina (in addition to Intelligence)" for their effect on Matter Creation and Time and Space and for easier implant design. Solitus Beta Genome (Int/Sense/Psy +7) is its best AI genome line.

Endgame HP monster, but AOWiki calls its Int and nano skills "poor" and breeds.json caps Int/Sense/Psychic at 400 with only 2 nano per Nano Pool point. Viable at 220 with full symbiants and perks - Atrox Secondary Genome returns Agi/Sense/Int/Psy +6 - but slow and expensive to cast bots on the way up.

AO-Universe MKIII rates Opifex for a damage-focused Engineer: "Best weapons. Highest pistol combo. Best Pistol/Grenade AR." Agility 544 / Sense 512 caps suit a pistol-and-evades build, at the cost of Int/Psy (464/448) - i.e. slower bots.

skillPriorities.why: Cost factor 1.0 (the Engineer's cheapest tier). EVERY bot summon requires MC and Time & Space at the SAME value: Feeble Automaton (43325) MC>4/TS>4, Predator M-30 (301855) MC>889/TS>889, Widowmaker Battle Drone (223323) MC>1895/TS>1890. MC also gates the auras, the pet heals and the special-attack absorbers. The single most important Engineer skill.

skillPriorities.target: max - always, keep level with MC
skillPriorities.why: Cost factor 1.0. The other half of every bot summon. Because a bot checks BOTH at the same number, the LOWER of MC/TS is your real bot level - a point of MC above TS is a wasted point. Also on the auras, pet heals, Shadowland Safeguard recall and Beacon Warp.

Cost factor 1.0. Third skill on every aura: EngineerAuras (strain 227) and EngineerDebuffAuras (strain 236) all need MC + MM + TS at the same value (Sympathetic Fortress Screen 154562 and Null Space Disruptor 154725 want ~870 each). MM also drives the team armor line (Gift of Assurance 227680: MC>1839, MM>1844), the damage shields and Boosted Tendons.

skillPriorities.target: high - to the buff tier you want
skillPriorities.why: Cost factor 2.4 (expensive) but it gates EVERY Engineer tradeskill and weapon buff: the five Mastery nanos (Electrical Engineering Mastery 227663 PM>817 through Weapon Smithing Mastery 227671 PM>854, +125 each), Engineer Composite Specialist Tradeskills (273346, PM>1033, +200 ME/EE/QFT) and Extreme Prejudice (29762, PM>647, +120 Grenade/+120 Pistol/+50 Heavy Weapons). Fund it to a chosen tier, not to max.
Cost factor 2.4. Paired 1:1 with PM on every Engineer buff line, so the lower of PM/SI is what you can actually cast. No Engineer buff wants SI without PM or vice versa.

skillPriorities.target: medium - to the pet-heal tier you want
skillPriorities.why: Cost factor 2.4. Only needed for the pet-repair line: Quick Fix (116793) MC/TS>83 BM>69, through A Maker's Touch (116791) MC/TS>841 BM>760, plus Master's Repairs (CompleteHealingLine, MC>925/TS>925/BM>836). BM always sits BELOW the MC/TS number on the same nano, so it never drives the build - top it to the heal you want and stop.

Cost factor 1.3 - cheap for an Engineer. AOWiki Engineer:Breed_and_Skills lists it under always-max ("needed for many things"); it drives NCU, belts and grid. The NCU Extensions perk adds +100 on top.
Cost factor 1.2 - the Engineer is one of the cheapest professions at it. AOWiki: max it "for implants at lower levels". The Unknown Factor perk adds +160 cumulative.

skillPriorities.skill: Mechanical Engineering (125) / Electrical Engineering (126) / Quantum FT (157) / Weapon Smithing (158)
skillPriorities.target: high - all four are cost factor 1.0 for the Engineer alone
skillPriorities.why: All four sit at 1.0 for the Engineer and at 2.0-2.5 for the Meta-Physicist; no other profession has all four in the cheapest tier. On top of the cheap IP the Engineer stacks Gadgeteer (+55/+55/+55/+70), Mechanic (+80/+80/+80/+130), Tinkerer (+65 ME/EE/QFT), Illogical Patterns (+160 to all four plus Tutoring) and its own Knowledge (+80) / Mastery (+125) / Composite Specialist (+200) nanos. Tradeskilling is not a side note for this class.
Cost factor 1.0 for the Engineer - the same tier as the nano schools - and +160 from Illogical Patterns. Cheap to keep maxed.
Cost 1.2 / 1.5. Needed for stims, kits and the Alchemist perk line. The Unknown Factor adds +160 to both; Philosopher's Stone (29772) adds +62/+62.

Cost factor 1.5 - by far the cheapest weapon skill the Engineer has (Grenade and Heavy Weapons are 2.0; Assault Rifle and Ranged Energy 3.0; Shotgun 3.2; Rifle and Bow 4.0). 9 of the 13 profession-locked Engineer weapon models in engineer-weapons-endgame.json are pistols (Augmented Master Engineer Pistol 274973, Dust Brigade Engineer Pistol 274559, Pistol of the Maker 214268, Pistol of the Creator 214269 ...). Backed by the Pistol Mastery perk line (+200), the Pistol Mastery nano (29246, +40) and Extreme Prejudice (+120).
Cost factor 2.0. The other Engineer-locked weapon family (the Nizno's Bomb Blaster line, 253228-253233). Supported by Demolitions (+200), Extreme Prejudice (29762, +120) and Creative Mind (+51).
Cost factor 1.6. Bots and auras are long casts and you re-summon after every bot death; Creative Mind adds +100 and the InitiativeBuffs line (Rapid Weapon) helps.

Cost factor 1.5 - cheap for an Engineer, and the main defence against being stripped, rooted or nano-debuffed (which also stops you summoning a fresh bot). The Notum Repulsor perk adds a large amount on top.
Cost factor 1.6. AOWiki Engineer:Breed_and_Skills lists Treatment under always-max ("heal kits and implants"). First Aid perk +40, Combat Knowledge +64.
Cost factor 1.8 - noticeably more expensive for an Engineer than for an MP or NT, who pay 1.0. Bots and auras are costly to cast. AOWiki lists it under "raise as needed" for survivability.
Cost factor 2.4. The Engineer has no self-heal nano - only the Bio Shielding perk actions - so HP is your buffer while the bot holds aggro. AOWiki puts it in "raise as needed".

Costs are 2.2 / 2.5 / 4.0 - unusually lopsided. Duck-Exp is the cheap one (and Creative Mind adds +51 to it); Evade-ClsC at 4.0 is among the most expensive skills in the whole Engineer column, so do not try to max it. AOWiki: raise evades so you are not "critted every time".
Cost factor 1.6. The AOWiki Engineer Guide notes raising it to 80 unlocks the important map upgrades.
Cost factor 2.0. AO-Universe Engineer Guide MKIII: "The runspeed of your pets is your own runspeed*1.2" - your Run Speed directly sets how fast the bot repositions, and pet commands only reach 50 m.
All three cost 1.6 for an Engineer versus 2.5 for a Meta-Physicist, and the Motorist perk adds +90 each. Cheap travel utility if you want it.

_perkCoverage.method: Every perk AOID in AOBuddy/GameData/Perks.xml (992 entries across 118 distinct perk lines) was probed against items.ocp with tools/mp-weapon-extractor (--probe-ids --probe-only). A perk line is Engineer-trainable when its perk items' ToWear action either carries "Profession EqualTo 3" or carries NO Profession requirement at all. Per-rank minimum level = the ToWear "Level GreaterThan N" + 1; per-rank bonuses = the OnWear Modify (53045) functions; granted special actions = the func53182 argument ids resolved against itemnames.sql.
_perkCoverage.note: 8 of the 44 lines are breed genome lines and only the 2 matching your breed are trainable, so one Engineer character can reach 38 of these 44. The 12 LE research proc perks are listed separately in the perks array: they are NOT perk templates in Perks.xml or items.ocp, so their ranks and numbers could not be read from local data.
_perkCoverage.coverageStatement: 44 of 44 Engineer-trainable perk lines enumerated, with every rank (345 ranks total), every rank's minimum level, every rank's stat bonuses and every granted special action, all from local client data. 12 of 12 Engineer LE research procs listed by name and research line, with NO local numbers - that is the one gap.

_unverified: LE research proc perks: the 12 LEProcEngineer* names come from AOSharp.Common/GameData/PerkHash.cs and the line/level mapping from wiki.aodb.us Engineer:Research_Lines. None of them appear in Perks.xml or items.ocp, so their proc chance, effect size, duration and offensive/defensive classification are NOT verified from local data.

Name conflict: PerkHash.cs has LEProcEngineerReactiveArmor, but wiki.aodb.us Engineer:Research_Lines names the Practical Application level-8 proc "Joint Discharge Array" and shows no perk called "Reactive Armor". Both names are recorded; which is the live in-game name is unresolved.

Per-research-level stat bonuses for the seven Engineer LE lines (Int +25; Sta +5/+10/+20 and Max Health +50/+100; Agi +25; Str +15/+20/+25; NCU +4 and Int +5/+20) come from wiki.aodb.us only - there is no local research data file in this repo.

The SL / AI / general grouping of perk lines is NOT an explicit flag in the client data. Perk templates carry only Profession, Level, Breed and the previous-rank chain. The grouping here is inferred from the min-level signature (AI lines repeat levels: 25/25/25/25/70/70/95/95/165/207 for the general AI lines and 15/15/55/55/55/105/105/145/205/210 for the AI profession lines) corroborated by the AOSharp PerkLine enum ordering and AOWiki naming. The Alien-Experience-level requirement itself is not present in the perk item.

Counterweight client-data anomaly: ranks 1-3 carry "Profession EqualTo 3" (Engineer), but ranks 4, 5 and 6 carry "Profession EqualTo 0" in its place (Adventurer/Enforcer/Shade unchanged). Engineer access to Counterweight ranks 4-6 is therefore NOT verified from the client data.

Perk bonuses are recorded per rank from each rank item's own OnWear Modify list; cumulativeBonusesAtMaxRank is the SUM across ranks. Whether AO applies perk rank bonuses cumulatively or replaces per rank was not verified from client data - the per-rank values in each perk's "ranks" array are the raw, unambiguous figures.

Alien Technology Expertise has 3 template ids in Perks.xml all named "Alien Technology Expertise 1", showing only 2 distinct level gates (15 and 75). The true rank count of that line is not resolvable from local data.

reference/breeds.json uses _breedStatValues Solitus=0 / Opifex=1 / Nanomage=2 / Atrox=3, but the client perk data and AOSharp.Common/GameData/Breed.cs use Solitus=1 / Opifex=2 / Nanomage=3 / Atrox=4. The genome perk entries here use the AOSharp/client numbering; breeds.json may need correcting.

The FalseProfession line (strain 218) is NOT an Engineer line. All three nanos - False Profession: Engineer (32034), Assume Profession: Engineer (117224), Mimic Profession: Engineer (117213) - require "Profession == 5" (AGENT) to cast and set VisualProfession(368) to 3 while applying a -5% to -25% penalty to all six nano schools. They appear in engineer-nanos.json only because that file's castability criterion accepts VisualProfession(368)==3. They are an Agent faking an Engineer.

Assault Rifle is commonly cited as an endgame Engineer weapon in the community, but nothing local supports it: AR costs 3.0 for an Engineer, no Engineer-locked AR exists in engineer-weapons-endgame.json (all 13 locked models are pistols or grenade launchers), no Engineer nano buffs AR, and the only AR-relevant perk line (Champion of Heavy Artillery) is open to every profession. Treat an AR Engineer as a community build, not a data-derived one.
One perk AOID present in Perks.xml was not found in items.ocp (991 of 992 probed); the missing template was not identified.
Exact IP costs per skill point at a given title level are not computed here - reference/skillcaps.json supplies cost FACTORS only, and its own _capComputationNote flags the cap curve as future work.

reference/skillcaps.json's own _dependencyReliability note flags the ability-dependency strings (e.g. which abilities feed Nano Pool and Body Dev.) as best-effort; only the cost arrays are cross-checked. Any ability-to-skill reasoning above leans on the cost factors, not those strings.
